key_insight: The paper introduces a scalable way to diagnose quantum reservoir quality using a task-independent expressivity score (ORS) and a task-dependent effective rank, separating “how expressive” a reservoir is from “how useful” its features are.
engineering_relevance: This gives practitioners a hardware-agnostic, low-overhead metric to compare reservoir families and predict when a quantum reservoir is likely to improve downstream machine-learning performance.
method: ORS scores expressivity by comparing only the largest output probabilities to an analytical Haar-random baseline.
Effective rank R_eff measures how much input-dependent information survives into the readout feature matrix.
A closed-form depolarizing-noise correction makes ORS usable on noisy hardware without full distribution reconstruction.
evidence_signal: The authors validate ORS against established complexity diagnostics, test robustness under simulated noise, and demonstrate it on IBM quantum hardware across synthetic and real quantum ELM/QRC benchmarks.
watch_item: ORS is informative about intrinsic expressivity, but predictive value still depends on the task and readout, so reservoir choice alone does not guarantee good performance.
paper_title: Diagnosing quantum reservoirs at scale based on expressivity and coverage
